title: Custom AI-accelerator XPU silicon clears $20B-per-quarter run-rate by Q4 2026
body: Custom AI-accelerator silicon — the hyperscaler-designed XPUs and ASICs that Broadcom and its peers fabricate as an alternative to merchant GPUs — is on track to clear a roughly $20 billion quarterly revenue run-rate at Broadcom alone by the close of calendar 2026, with a parallel disclosure that the count of named core custom-silicon customers moves past six. The Broadcom fiscal Q2 print is the trigger: AI-semiconductor revenue of $10.8 billion grew 143% year over year, Q3 was guided to approximately $16 billion at over 200% growth, and bookings for AI semiconductors topped $30 billion in a single quarter against the $10.8 billion actually shipped. A backlog that pre-commits nearly three times current shipments is not a demand pull that decays gracefully; it is capacity that has already been sold, so the shipped-revenue line tends to climb toward the booked line rather than away from it. If Q3 lands near $16 billion as guided, the sequential slope plus the disclosed backlog puts the following quarter within reach of the $20 billion mark. The same dynamic pressures the customer roster: six core XPU customers were enough to book $30 billion in a quarter, and the economics of a single hyperscaler custom-silicon program — amortizing design cost against captive internal inference and training demand — are now visibly favorable enough that additional named programs graduating from development to volume is the path of least resistance. The forward state to watch is therefore both a revenue threshold and a roster expansion, either of which confirms that the custom-ASIC track is no longer a niche hedge against GPU allocation but a structurally compounding second supply line for accelerator compute.

reasoning.because: Broadcom Q2 AI-semi revenue hit $10.8B (+143% YoY), Q3 guided ~$16B, >$30B booked vs $10.8B shipped
reasoning.given: A backlog pre-committing ~3x shipments is sold capacity, so shipped revenue climbs toward booked
reasoning.so_that: Custom XPU/ASIC silicon clears a ~$20B/quarter run-rate at one supplier and the core-customer count passes six
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026; a vendor AI-semi quarter near $20B or a 7th core XPU customer
reasoning.plain_language: Companies designing their own AI chips already ordered about three times what they bought last quarter, so those chips will soon sell far more.

summary: Broadcom's fiscal Q2 put custom AI-accelerator (XPU) revenue at $10.8B, up 143%, with Q3 guided near $16B and over $30B booked against $10.8B shipped. That sold-out backlog pushes shipped revenue toward a roughly $20B quarterly run-rate by Q4 2026, likely past today's six named core XPU customers.
